audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet expanded dwelling, floating axe head, Aramean intelligence conflict, Dothan vision, induced blindness, merciful feeding, and Samaria siege narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for communal expansion, borrowed-tool liability, miracle object recovery, military intelligence, servant fear and chariot vision, blindness terminology, prisoner treatment, siege famine, child cannibalism report, royal blame, and prophetic threat.

verses.restored: Sons of prophets said to Elisha, Look, place where we dwell before you is too narrow for us.

familiar.text: And the sons of the prophets said unto Elisha, Behold now, the place where we dwell with thee is too strait for us.

verses.restored: Let us go, please, to Jordan and take from there each man one beam, and make for ourselves there a place to dwell. He said, Go.

familiar.text: Let us go, we pray thee, unto Jordan, and take thence every man a beam, and let us make us a place there, where we may dwell. And he answered, Go ye.

verses.restored: One said, Please be willing and go with your servants. He said, I will go.

familiar.text: And one said, Be content, I pray thee, and go with thy servants. And he answered, I will go.

verses.restored: He went with them, and they came to Jordan and cut trees.

familiar.text: So he went with them. And when they came to Jordan, they cut down wood.

verses.restored: It was, when one was felling the beam, that iron fell into water. He cried and said, Ah, my lord! And it was borrowed.

familiar.text: But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water: and he cried, and said, Alas, master! for it was borrowed.

verses.restored: Man of Divine said, Where did it fall? He showed him place. He cut a stick, threw it there, and made iron float.

familiar.text: And the man of God said, Where fell it? And he shewed him the place. And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did swim.

verses.restored: He said, Lift it for yourself. He stretched out his hand and took it.

familiar.text: Therefore said he, Take it up to thee. And he put out his hand, and took it.

verses.restored: King of Aram was fighting against Israel, and he counseled with his servants, saying, At such and such place shall be my camp.

familiar.text: Then the king of Syria warred against Israel, and took counsel with his servants, saying, In such and such a place shall be my camp.

verses.restored: Man of Divine sent to king of Israel, saying, Guard yourself from passing this place, for there Arameans are descending.

familiar.text: And the man of God sent unto the king of Israel, saying, Beware that thou pass not such a place; for thither the Syrians are come down.

verses.restored: King of Israel sent to place man of Divine told him and warned him about, and he guarded himself there, not once or twice.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God told him and warned him of, and saved himself there, not once nor twice.

verses.restored: Heart of king of Aram stormed over this matter. He called his servants and said to them, Will you not tell me who among us is for king of Israel?

familiar.text: Therefore the heart of the king of Syria was sore troubled for this thing; and he called his servants, and said unto them, Will ye not shew me which of us is for the king of Israel?

verses.restored: One of his servants said, No, my lord king; but Elisha prophet who is in Israel tells king of Israel words you speak in chamber of your lying down.

familiar.text: And one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber.

verses.restored: He said, Go and see where he is, and I will send and take him. It was told to him, saying, Look, he is in Dothan.

familiar.text: And he said, Go and spy where he is, that I may send and fetch him. And it was told him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothan.

verses.restored: He sent there horses, chariots, and a heavy force; they came by night and surrounded city.

familiar.text: Therefore sent he thither horses, and chariots, and a great host: and they came by night, and compassed the city about.

verses.restored: Servant of man of Divine rose early and went out, and look, a force surrounded city with horses and chariots. His young man said to him, Ah, my lord, what shall we do?

familiar.text: And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?

verses.restored: He said, Do not fear, for more are those with us than those with them.

familiar.text: And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.

verses.restored: Elisha prayed and said, YHWH, please open his eyes so he may see. YHWH opened eyes of young man, and he saw, and look, mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.

familiar.text: And Elisha prayed, and said, LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.

verses.restored: They came down to him, and Elisha prayed to YHWH and said, Please strike this nation with blindness/confusion. He struck them with blindness/confusion according to word of Elisha.

familiar.text: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed unto the LORD, and said, Smite this people, I pray thee, with blindness. And he smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.

verses.restored: Elisha said to them, This is not the way and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to man whom you seek. He led them to Samaria.

familiar.text: And Elisha said unto them, This is not the way, neither is this the city: follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom ye seek. But he led them to Samaria.

verses.restored: It was, when they came to Samaria, that Elisha said, YHWH, open eyes of these so they may see. YHWH opened their eyes, and they saw, and look, they were in midst of Samaria.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when they were come into Samaria, that Elisha said, LORD, open the eyes of these men, that they may see. And the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw; and, behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.

verses.restored: King of Israel said to Elisha when he saw them, Shall I strike, shall I strike, my father?

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said unto Elisha, when he saw them, My father, shall I smite them? shall I smite them?

verses.restored: He said, You shall not strike. Would you strike those whom you captured with your sword and bow? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their lord.

familiar.text: And he answered, Thou shalt not smite them: wouldest thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.

verses.restored: He prepared for them a great feast; they ate and drank, and he sent them away, and they went to their lord. Bands of Aram did not continue to enter land of Israel.

familiar.text: And he prepared great provision for them: and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.

verses.restored: It was after this that Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his camp, went up, and besieged Samaria.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after this, that Benhadad king of Syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged Samaria.

verses.restored: There was great famine in Samaria. Look, they besieged it until head of donkey was for eighty silver and fourth of a qab of dove's dung/seedpods for five silver.

familiar.text: And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.

verses.restored: It was, when king of Israel was passing upon wall, that a woman cried to him, saying, Save, my lord king!

familiar.text: And as the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, there cried a woman unto him, saying, Help, my lord, O king.

verses.restored: He said, If YHWH does not save you, from where shall I save you—from threshing floor or winepress?

familiar.text: And he said, If the LORD do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?

verses.restored: King said to her, What is for you? She said, This woman said to me, Give your son and we will eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.

familiar.text: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow.

verses.restored: So we cooked my son and ate him. I said to her on next day, Give your son and we will eat him, but she hid her son.

familiar.text: So we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said unto her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she hath hid her son.

verses.restored: It was, when king heard words of woman, that he tore his garments while passing on wall, and people saw, and look, sackcloth was beneath upon his flesh.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he rent his clothes; and he passed by upon the wall, and the people looked, and, behold, he had sackcloth within upon his flesh.

verses.restored: He said, Thus may Divine do to me and thus add, if head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains upon him today.

familiar.text: Then he said, God do so and more also to me, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat shall stand on him this day.

verses.restored: Elisha was sitting in his house, and elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man from before him. Before messenger came to him, he said to elders, Do you see that this son of murderer has sent to remove my head? See, when messenger comes, shut door and press him with door. Is not sound of feet of his lord behind him?

familiar.text: But Elisha sat in his house, and the elders sat with him; and the king sent a man from before him: but ere the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, See ye how this son of a murderer hath sent to take away mine head? look, when the messenger cometh, shut the door, and hold him fast at the door: is not the sound of his master’s feet behind him?

verses.restored: While he was still speaking with them, look, messenger came down to him, and king said, Look, this evil is from YHWH; why should I wait for YHWH any longer?

familiar.text: And while he yet talked with them, behold, the messenger came down unto him: and he said, Behold, this evil is of the LORD; what should I wait for the LORD any longer?

translation_notes: The sons of prophets need more living space and organize collective labor. Spiritual community still requires housing, tools, land access, and practical planning.
The lost axe head matters because it was borrowed. The small miracle centers liability, poverty, and restoration of another person's property rather than spectacle.
Military intelligence attributed to Elisha protects Israel but also turns prophetic knowledge into a wartime asset; this must not authorize surveillance claims or leader omniscience.
The servant's opened eyes are a reassurance scene, not proof that every danger is secretly surrounded by supernatural force or that fear is irrational.
The Hebrew term in verses 18 and 20 may imply dazzlement, confusion, or impaired perception rather than ordinary blindness. It must not support stigma against blind people.
Elisha forbids execution of the captured Arameans and commands food and water. Feeding enemies interrupts a cycle of killing and produces a period without raids.
The later royal siege shows the truce did not permanently end interstate war. One act of mercy is still ethically meaningful even when it does not guarantee lasting peace.
The famine prices portray extreme scarcity; the precise term translated dove's dung may refer to a plant or seedpod and requires lexical audit.
The two mothers' story is siege atrocity and starvation trauma. The woman whose son was eaten is not morally responsible for conditions created by war and famine.
The king redirects grief and rage toward Elisha. Leaders must not scapegoat prophets, civilians, minorities, or critics for systemic catastrophe.
safety_note: Do not use the vision or blindness scene to stigmatize disability, claim supernatural surveillance, or manipulate frightened people. Do not blame starving parents for siege atrocities. Center borrowed-property restoration, fear met with reassurance, prisoners fed rather than killed, and political responsibility for famine and war.
